description: HRS §235-53 requires the Director-prescribed tax table for nonitemizers up to a Director-determined ceiling that is not less than $20,000.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module never represented HRS 235-53, so it published section 235-51 schedule tax for every nonitemizer, including those whose taxable income does not exceed the Director's ceiling (statutorily at least $20,000), for whom the statute imposes the Director-prescribed table tax "in lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51".
triage.triage_notes: Read the provisions through the pinned corpus: us-hi/statute/235-53 (confirms "In lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51" for nonitemizers whose taxable income "does not exceed the ceiling amount", ceiling "not less than $20,000"), us-hi/statute/235-55.7 (confirms (d) "If a rental unit is occupied by two or more individuals, and more than one individual is able to qualify as a claimant, the claim for credit shall be based upon a pro rata share of the rent paid"), and us-hi/statute/235-55.6 (confirms (c) the dollar limit "shall be reduced by the aggregate amount excludable from gross income under section 129", and (d)(1)(A)/(B) earned-income limit keyed to being married at the close of the year). This is a MULTI-DEFECT single-module commit; I picked the 235-53 hold as decisive because the PR body devotes its whole "Source boundary" section to it and the diff adds the citation path, the $20,000 ceiling parameter, the hold judgment, the waiver entry, and the profile gate. Other independent fidelity corrections in the same diff, any of which a reviewer could split out: (1) hi_pit_2026_cdcc_creditable_expenses changed from max(0, min(expenses, cap) - assistance_exclusion) to min(expenses, max(0, cap - assistance_exclusion), earned-income limit) — the pre-fix form reduced the expenses rather than the 235-55.6(c) dollar limit and understated the credit whenever expenses were below the cap (amount_mismatch); (2) the same rule's earned-income limit now applies the two-earner minimum only when joint AND not a surviving spouse, since a surviving spouse is not married at the close of the year under 235-55.6(d)(1) (wrong_entity_or_scope); (3) hi_pit_2026_refundable_low_income_renter_credit now divides cash rent by the qualified-claimant count before the $1,000 test, encoding 235-55.7(d), which was absent (unrepresented_clause); (4) hi_pit_2026_capital_gains_worksheet_line_10 dropped the Hawaii long/short-term gain adjustments and the Form N-158 line 4e subtraction, which had been caller-completed amounts with no in-module grounding, replacing them with boolean holds (untraceable_branch / completed-result inputs); (5) hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_net_income_tax_liability dropped the max(0, ...) floor so refundable credits can drive liability negative — note the pre-fix module did publish a separate refundable-excess output (now made private), so the floor was arguably a presentation choice rather than lost information; (6) new domain bound age_65_exemption_count <= 2 from 235-54(a). Changes that are NOT defects: married-filing-separately moved from a hold to a supported filing status (added scope, plus the matching filing-status exclusivity logic), the decomposition of composite caller judgments into granular raw facts (CDCC conditions, EITC status/dependents match, renter occupancy/property-tax conditions, food/renter exemption presence-failure counts), and the new public hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits stage. Follow-ups in the same PR: 26ebd1a18 "Tighten Hawaii tax-table and MFS holds" later REMOVED the `taxable_income <= ceiling` condition from hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies (because only the statutory minimum of the Director's ceiling is known, so all nonitemizers must fail closed) and moved the hold out of supported_profile_applies into the public tax/liability stages, and also re-held MFS food/renter claims; 249e8e6f6 "Prevent Hawaii food credit child overlap" followed. So this commit's 235-53 fix was correct in kind but too narrow, and was widened one commit later. Commit message body is empty; the PR body is the whole-PR body, which is why confidence is 0.75 rather than higher.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute the label and could not: the pre-fix file at e97d5848 contains no mention of "235-53" or any tax table (verified by grep over the full 2261-line pre file), yet its supported profile already required `not hi_pit_2026_elects_itemized_deductions`, so every publicly published taxpayer was a nonitemizer and the public `hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_before_credits` returned the §235-51 schedule/alt-tax `hi_pit_2026_income_tax_liability` for all of them. The pinned corpus text of HRS 235-53(a)(1) reads "In lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51, there is hereby imposed ... (A) Who does not itemize ... and (B) Whose taxable income for such taxable year does not exceed the ceiling amount, a tax determined under tables ... prescribed by the director", with (a)(2) fixing the ceiling at "the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director" — a mandatory substitution, not an election, so the pre-fix published amount disagrees with the source for that population. The fix adds the missing clause (new §235-53 citation path, `hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` = 20000, the `hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies` condition, and the gate in `supported_profile_applies`), which is exactly unrepresented_clause; "mechanical" and "not_a_defect" both fail because formulas, inputs, outputs and the profile gate all changed and the module previously claimed this population rather than disclaiming it.
triage.verifier_notes: Cross-checks a reviewer should know. (1) Boundary strictness of the new hold is right, not a second defect: the statute says "does not exceed the ceiling amount" and the added rule uses `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling`. But the ceiling parameter is pinned at the statutory *minimum* ($20,000) while §235-53(a)(2) lets the director set any amount "not less than $20,000"; taxpayers between $20,000 and the director's actual ceiling are therefore still published under §235-51, so the fix only partially represents the clause — a residual, not a reason to downgrade the label. (2) This is a multi-defect repair commit, so the corpus entry is not one-defect-per-module-change. Other independent fidelity fixes in the same diff, each a different kind: capital-gain worksheet line 10 drops the Hawaii long/short-term adjustments and the `- hi_pit_2026_form_n_158_line_4e` subtraction (re-grounding, untraceable_branch); `hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_net_income_tax_liability` loses its `max(0, ...)` floor so the signed liability can go negative (boundary/polarity); CDCC creditable expenses re-nest min/max so the assistance exclusion no longer reduces the already-capped expense (polarity_or_logic); the renter credit gains the statutory "pro rata share of the rent paid" divisor (another unrepresented_clause); MFS is added to the supported scope by deleting `and not hi_pit_2026_is_married_filing_separately` (wrong_entity_or_scope); and a new age-65 exemption cap of 2 bounds the input domain (amount/domain). If the corpus wants a single canonical kind per entry, the §235-53 hold is a defensible pick (it is the PR body's headline "Source boundary" and matches the supplied rule_path), but the entry should be flagged as bundled. (3) Provenance caveat: commit a8ca13eee7 is an intra-PR repair inside PR #1035 "Add Hawaii 2026 resident tax bounded core" (merged 2026-07-24), so the defective state existed only on the unmerged branch and was caught by the review-fix cycle — never in merged rulespec-us content. If the corpus is meant to hold defects that reached main, this case is branch-internal. (4) Weakest alternative kind considered: untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision"), on the theory that nonitemizer tax was grounded on §235-51 instead of §235-53. I rejected it because the §235-51 branch is genuinely grounded and is left intact for its correct population; nothing is removed or re-grounded, a condition is added. wrong_entity_or_scope is the second-best alternative (the published population was too broad), but scope narrowing is the remedy here, not the defect.
